bugs.title: Expanded chat view shows the paged-file directive as the body of any URL/binary file that follows a paged file in the same prompt
bugs.description: The chat renderer's body-recovery is index-misaligned when a paged file (which emits TWO <file> blocks — head + directive — but only ONE FileDetail) precedes a detail that has no length-derived offsets. computeDetailOffsets (file-injector.ts:475) only computes contentStart/contentLen for kind 'text' and 'paged'; url and binary details fall through to the tier-3 regex fallback bodies[i] (file-injector.ts:1065-1067), which pairs the i-th DETAIL with the i-th <file> BLOCK. After a paged file the block list is one longer than the detail list, so the following URL/binary detail pairs with the paged DIRECTIVE block instead of its own block. Verified with the real renderer: prompt `#@big.log and #@note.bin` under a tight budget → expanded view contains '<paged: ...>' twice and never shows 'binary file — contents not injected'; prompt `#@big.log and #example.com/doc' → the URL's expanded view shows the <paged:> directive instead of the extracted markdown. Collapsed read-lines and the model-facing message.content are correct — this is display-only, but it shows visibly wrong content for a prompt mix the spec explicitly supports ('#@file.txt and #example.com in same prompt', URL spec §7; PRD §10 rows 'Chat display — binary ... expanded shows the same note text'; URL spec §6 'Expanded view shows the extracted markdown').
bugs.reproduction: 1. Create big.log (~120KB, e.g. 3000 lines × 30 chars) and note.bin (bytes 00 01 02). 2. Load the extension; use a model/context where remaining budget forces paging (e.g. ctx.getContextUsage → window 40000). 3. Submit `Summarize #@big.log and inspect #@note.bin`. 4. Press ctrl+o to expand the green injected-files box. 5. Observed: the binary's body area shows '<paged: 118890 chars; head delivered 212 complete lines; read the rest ...>' (the directive belonging to big.log) and the directive appears twice; the binary note text never appears. Same with `#@big.log and #example.com/doc` — the URL body shows the directive, not the page markdown. Root cause: computeDetailOffsets skips kind url/binary (line 475), so renderInjectedMessage falls to bodies[i] (line 1067) whose indices count BLOCKS (2 per paged file) while i counts DETAILS (1 per paged file).
bugs.location: file-injector.ts:475 (computeDetailOffsets skips url/binary kinds) and file-injector.ts:1065-1067 (tier-3 bodies[i] index pairing)

bugs.title: Malformed line-range tokens inside delivered markdown files are silently verbatim and leak an unresolved raw token into injectFile (process-cwd stat, relative block name)
bugs.description: LR-3 requires malformed ranges (e.g. `#@x.md:0`, `#@x.md:5-3`) to be left verbatim AND reported with a hasUI-guarded warning notify. That works at the top level (processTokenStream checks rec.invalidRange, file-injector.ts:1243-1247), but a malformed range found while scanning a DELIVERED markdown file takes a different path: injectMarkdown's Step-5 loop (file-injector.ts:1558-1561) does NOT check rec.invalidRange and calls injectFile(rec.path, ...) where rec.path is the RAW UNRESOLVED token string (pushed at file-injector.ts:1193). Consequences: (a) no warning notify is emitted — the malformed marker vanishes silently inside markdown, unlike top level, contradicting LR-3 'malformed ranges are not silent'; (b) injectFile fs.stat()s the raw token against the PROCESS cwd (neither the markdown's directory nor ctx.cwd resolution applies), so if a file literally named e.g. `a.md:0` happens to exist in the process working directory it is injected with a RELATIVE block name — verified: block `<file name="a.md:0">\nliteral colon md\n</file>` — violating §6.1 'Use the absolute resolved path as name' and the §4.5 rule that markdown imports resolve relative to the importing file's directory.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Create bad.md containing `see #@a.md:0 here`, plus a.md. 2. In a different directory used as the pi process cwd, create a literal file named `a.md:0` with some content. 3. Submit `#@bad.md` (with hasUI true and a notify spy). 4. Observed: injected=2 — bad.md plus the literal `a.md:0` file from the process cwd, emitted with a relative block name; and zero warning notifies for the malformed range. Without the literal colon-file: injected=1 and no warning (silent), whereas the same malformed token at the top level warns.
bugs.location: file-injector.ts:1558-1561 (injectMarkdown Step 5 loop missing invalidRange guard) fed by file-injector.ts:1193 (scanTokens pushes raw token as path for invalid ranges)

bugs.title: URL image response with empty body attaches an empty ImageContent (F5 guard not mirrored to the URL path)
bugs.description: The local-file image path guards 0-byte images (F5, file-injector.ts:1322-1333: 'a 0-byte image file would attach an EMPTY ImageContent (which providers reject)' → note block instead). The URL image path (file-injector.ts:921-937) has no such guard: a 200 response with content-type image/* and an empty body (or any body resizeImage reduces to nothing) results in state.images.push({ type:'image', data:'', mimeType }) — an empty ImageContent attached to the user message, exactly the provider-rejected shape F5 exists to prevent. Verified with a mocked fetch returning 200/image/png with empty body: injected=1, images[0].data.length === 0, block `<file name="https://example.com/empty.png"></file>`.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Mock a server responding 200, content-type image/png, zero-length body. 2. Submit `#example.com/empty.png` with the extension loaded. 3. Observed: the transform returns images=[{type:'image',data:'',mimeType:'image/png'}] — an empty attachment a provider may reject with a 400 that fails the whole turn, instead of the F5-style note the local path emits for the identical situation.
bugs.location: file-injector.ts:921-937 (injectUrl image branch lacks the F5 empty-body guard)

bugs.title: #@ autocomplete remap rewrites non-@ suggestion values to '#@<value>', contradicting its own pass-through guard
bugs.description: The autocomplete provider's value remap (file-injector.ts:1906) is `if (!v.startsWith("#@")) v = v.startsWith("@") ? "#" + v : "#@" + v;`. A suggestion whose value does not start with '@' (e.g. a slash-command '/cmd') becomes '#@/cmd' — mangled — even though the adjacent comment states the intent is to 'pass them through untouched so we don't mangle slash-command suggestions'. Only the prefix-level guard (`if (!inner.prefix.startsWith("@")) return inner;`) protects, which does not help when the built-in mixes @-file items with other items under an '@' prefix. Verified with a mocked current provider returning items [@a.ts, @ab.ts, /cmd] under prefix '@a': the /cmd item is returned as '#@/cmd'. Latent today (built-in @-queries normally return only @-prefixed values) but the defensive code contradicts its documented purpose.
bugs.reproduction: Drive the registered autocomplete provider (session_start handler with ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider) with a `current.getSuggestions` that returns { prefix:'@a', items:[{value:'@a.ts'},{value:'/cmd'}] } for the rewritten line. Await provider.getSuggestions(['review #@a'],0,10,{}). Observed: items[1].value === '#@/cmd' (expected: '/cmd' untouched).

bugs.title: ftp:// scheme tokens are never fetched, deviating from the PRD URL spec §2.2/§7 (documented-code narrowing to https?)
bugs.description: The PRD URL feature spec defines URL_SHAPE_RE with `(https?|ftp)` and its §7 edge table promises 'ftp:// scheme | supported by URL_SHAPE_RE; fetch via fetch (Node supports it)'. The shipped URL_SHAPE_RE (file-injector.ts:43) accepts only `(https?)`, so `#ftp://example.com/x` fails the shape gate and is left untouched (verified: zero fetch calls). Note this is an intentional narrowing documented in the code comment, and it is behaviorally near-identical in practice because Node's fetch/undici cannot actually fetch ftp:// (it would throw and fall back to verbatim anyway) — recorded as a literal spec deviation for completeness.
bugs.reproduction: Submit `#ftp://example.com/x` with a fetch spy. Observed: no candidate passes URL_SHAPE_RE, no fetch is attempted, token stays verbatim. PRD §2.2's literal regex includes ftp and §7 lists it as supported.

summary: Tested the pi-file-injector extension end-to-end against the full PRD (file #@ injection, line ranges LR-1..LR-7, markdown transitive imports, URL #injection, config, renderer) with a mix of: the repo's own suite (all 4 test files pass, typecheck clean), three custom jiti-loaded harnesses (~150 assertions), and a real `pi` runtime run via a mock OpenAI-compatible provider (verifying the verbatim user message, the fileInjector.injected custom message after it, session-file persistence as a custom_message entry, and stored '#@' preserved for cancel/fork re-triggering). The recently-fixed LR-1..LR-5 behaviors all hold: slices run the §5.5 budget/paging decision with file-coordinate resume offsets, images/binaries claim the bare abs (no duplicate bytes), malformed ranges warn at top level, past-EOF starts turn away with claim revocation, and clamped ends display the delivered range (:2-5). Markdown relative resolution, code-exemption, cycles, shorthand, bare-@ opt-in, config precedence, URL shape gate/deny-list/dedup/no-egress opt-out, budget sharing across files+URLs, and the autocomplete remap were all exercised and behave per spec. Five issues found: one major display bug (renderer expanded-view body misalignment after a paged file — wrong content shown for following URL/binary files) and four minor ones (markdown-level malformed ranges silently verbatim plus raw-token leak into injectFile; empty-body URL images attach an empty ImageContent; autocomplete remap mangles non-@ values contrary to its comment; ftp:// scheme dropped from the shape gate vs the PRD's literal regex). Model-facing delivery is correct in every case — all five are display/robustness/spec-parity issues, none corrupt the content the model receives.
recommendations: Fix BUG-001 by pairing tier-3 bodies with details through the same path-aware cursor logic computeDetailOffsets uses (or simply compute contentStart/contentLen for the url/binary kinds too — their blocks are body-bearing), so the expanded view can never mis-pair after a paged file.

In injectMarkdown's Step-5 loop, skip rec.invalidRange records exactly like processTokenStream does (and optionally emit the same LR-3 warning), which also removes the raw-token-into-injectFile leak (BUG-002).
Mirror the F5 empty-image guard into injectUrl's image branch (empty body → note block, no attachment) (BUG-003).
In the autocomplete item remap, leave values that do not start with '@' (or '#@') untouched (BUG-004).
Either document the https?-only narrowing in the README's Limits section or extend URL_SHAPE_RE to accept ftp:// and let the fetch fail to verbatim, so code and PRD text agree (BUG-005).
